description: Companies whose board still holds reverse-split authority it may use without another shareholder vote: an approval on file (shareholder vote or written consent; tracker states consent_pending, voted_approved, ratio_fixed) not past a stated expiry, one row per company (its newest approval; other live ones in otherLiveAuthorityEpisodeIds). Soonest stated expiry first. Each row is the Reverse Splits page row (ticker, companyName, ratio, exchange, approvalPath, domicile, splitAuthority, authorityTerms, sourceUrl / sourceAccession, sourceDocuments: every document behind the approval with accession or URL) plus an "authority" block: episodeId, state, approvedDate, approvedRatio {fixed, min, max} (the per-split ratio or range approved), cumulativeCap (cap on the product of every split drawn on it), multiStep, expiresOn, expiryTerm, daysUntilExpiry, and room: capRatio + capBasis ("cumulative_cap", or "single_split_maximum" = no cumulative cap stated and nothing drawn, so one split up to the approved maximum), perSplitMax, usedSplits + usedRatio (product of the splits already executed on it; 1 = none drawn), remainingRatio (capRatio / usedRatio), exhausted, nextSplitMax, pendingRatio (a ratio the board set that has not taken effect) and a one-line label. The approval route is approvalPath.path (shareholder_vote, written_consent, fpi_written_resolution, pre_approved_range, board_only, depositary_ratio_change or unknown = "Not determined", not "no vote"). Ratios are 1-for-N factors and combine by product. Not measured is not "none remaining": room.remainingRatio null comes with room.notMeasuredReason ("cumulative_cap_not_stated", "ratio_not_stated" or "drawn_split_ratio_not_stated"), meaning the remaining room is not measured for that reason. Such rows are listed, never dropped, and are not full. expiresOn null = the documents read state no expiry, not "never expires". An empty list is what the tracker has on file, not evidence that no board holds authority. This screen covers approvals on file; a board that may split under its statute or charter with no approval at all shows as splitAuthority.boardMayActWithoutVote on a row and in the per-company lifecycle, and is not listed here on that basis alone. Locked rows are withheld, not absent. The facts are part of Signal8 Pro: a key not owned by a Pro account gets rows with locked: true and only ticker, companyName, hasPage and exchange (access "preview", lockedCount). minRemaining and expiringBefore are Pro-only filters (on a non-Pro key they apply to unlocked rows only; filtersLimitedToUnlocked: true). A row whose remaining room or expiry is not measured never matches those filters; excludedNotMeasured counts how many were left out for that reason. Paging uses limit and nextCursor. available: false or an HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED = unavailable, and the response says nothing about any company. The data describes what is on file and carries no view on whether a split will happen, what it means for the price, or what anyone should do.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

exchange.description: Listing venues to keep: NASDAQ, NYSE, AMEX (NYSE American), OTC, or not_measured. Empty = every row.

expiringBefore.description: Keep rows whose stated expiresOn is before this YYYY-MM-DD day. Rows with no stated expiry never match.

minRemaining.description: Keep rows whose room.remainingRatio is at least this N (1-for-N), e.g. 50. Rows not measured never match.
